research_page.title: Alzheimer's drug development pipeline: 2026
research_page.description: An annual review of the Alzheimer's pipeline identifying 158 drugs across 192 trials, emphasizing disease-modifying therapies and biomarker integration.
research_page.takeaway_md: The 2026 pipeline is dominated by disease-modifying therapies and heavily integrates biomarkers for trial eligibility. While the review highlights a large volume of repurposed agents in Phase 2, this optimism must be balanced against high-profile Phase 3 failures of repurposed drugs that occurred shortly after this snapshot.
key_findings_md: The pipeline includes 158 candidate drugs in 192 active trials, a 40% increase over the past decade (paper, Abstract).
Disease-targeted therapies (DTTs) comprise 73% of the pipeline, evenly split between small molecules and biologics (paper, Results).
Biomarkers are now standard practice, featuring in 87% of Phase 3 and 89% of Phase 2 trials for eligibility or outcome tracking (paper, Results).
Repurposed drugs represent 35% of the pipeline, primarily driven by non-industry sponsors in earlier clinical phases (paper, Results).
research_page.methods_md: Systematic review of the clinicaltrials.gov registry to identify active interventional trials for Alzheimer's disease across all phases and disease stages, indexed as of January 1, 2026.
research_page.trial_evidence_md: As an annual pipeline review, this document maps the landscape rather than reporting new efficacy data. It underscores the clinical shift toward disease-modifying treatments following the successes of anti-amyloid biologics. However, the clinical evidence context reveals that the large "repurposed" pipeline segment is highly vulnerable, as demonstrated by the failure of semaglutide in the Phase 3 EVOKE trials shortly after this review was published.
research_page.sentiment_md: Public perception of the pipeline is deeply polarized. Mainstream media and institutions frequently frame the pipeline's growth and recent approvals as historic breakthroughs. In contrast, patient and retail investor communities exhibit profound skepticism, weighed down by the high costs, intensive safety monitoring requirements for ARIA, and the ultimately modest clinical benefits of currently approved therapies.
caveats_md: The pipeline snapshot is static as of January 1, 2026; major trial readouts occurring later in the year render some of its optimism—particularly around repurposed drugs—outdated.
The analysis relies exclusively on clinicaltrials.gov, meaning trials conducted solely outside North America may be omitted if they are not registered on the US platform.
Classifying therapies as disease-modifying versus symptomatic relies on the sponsors' stated therapeutic intent rather than proven mechanistic outcomes.
